detail.longDescription:
> There’s a bit of irony in the title. At the time of writing, Gliver, a Guile
based window manager for Wayland in the style of StumpWM and Emacs, isn’t yet in
Guix. There is, however, an open PR to add Gliver to Guix. However, what that
patch is really waiting on is an upcoming release of Gliver which will solve
many bugs. > > Notably, that release will be 0.0.5. If that sounds early, Gliver
still is early. There are bugs, and you will probably have to file issues for
some that you discover. There are also some noticeable missing features. But it
doesn’t matter. Gliver is everything I want from a desktop experience, and I
suspect for many of the kinds of people who read my blog, it will be for them as
well. > > Gliver might not be for everyone. But if the following appeals to you:
a live-hackable, written in Guile Scheme, tiling window manager which looks
good, feels good, and whose codebase is understandable and, indeed, encourages
you to understand and explore it, Gliver is for you. StumpWM
[https://stumpwm.github.io/] was what I ended up after over 30 years with as my
preferred Window manager, and what suits me best. It is extremely fast for
software development because with its manual tiling, you can pair docs, browser,
command line, editor and config side by side and switch with one key press. It
is written in Common Lisp, has Emacs-like key chords, and is entirely
programmable (for example you can bind a key to a function that copies the URL
of the current browser window, invokes Emacs, and pastes that URL into a
“bookmarks.org [http://bookmarks.org]” file). A window manager like this,
written in Guile, running under Wayland, is a dream coming true.
